title: Sant Attar Singh
hook: a holy man of Mastuana who founded schools

segments.voice: Yesterday, Jail Letters, and your line was kirtan in prison. Did a steady song carry you through something heavy? Today closes a week that began on the railway at Panja Sahib. Day nine hundred ninety-four.

Crowds come to hear him sing kirtan. He's known for long hours of meditation, and people call him a sant. So when something is built at Mastuana, in the Punjab countryside, beside his name, you might expect a gurdwara with a gold dome and marble floors. There is a gurdwara. But there is also a school, and then a college. Classrooms, teachers, books, and children learning Gurmukhi beside arithmetic. Today: Sant Attar Singh.
screen: `CROWDS FOR KIRTAN.` → `NOT ONLY A GURDWARA.` → `A SCHOOL AT MASTUANA.`

segments.voice: First, the sant. Attar Singh served as a soldier as a young man, and then left that life for one of devotion. He became known across Punjab as a sant, a holy man, who spent long hours in meditation and kirtan and traveled to preach the Gurus' teaching. Tradition says that people took amrit, the Khalsa initiation, after hearing him. Second, the turn. His followers remember him wanting faith and learning to grow together. At Mastuana he founded a school and a college, the Akal College, where Gurmukhi and the Gurus' teaching were taught alongside ordinary subjects. That's today's line: schools, not only temples. Third, the reach. Tradition says he was invited to lay a foundation stone for Banaras Hindu University, a sign of how widely he was respected beyond the Sikh community. He supported education conferences in Punjab, too. Fourth, the root. In the Japji, at Ang 2 of the Guru Granth Sahib, Guru Nanak says that within the mind are gems, jewels and rubies, if a person listens to the Guru's teaching even once. Some readers hear his schools in that line: there are jewels in a child's mind, and a school is one way to help them be found. And that closes this week: Panja Sahib's train, Jaito's long campaign, the Gurdwara Act, Master Tara Singh, the Rehat Maryada, Jail Letters, written in his cell, and now a sant who built classrooms. Reform, it turns out, needed both courage and chalk.
screen: `A SOLDIER BECOMES A SANT.` · `A SCHOOL AT MASTUANA.` · `RESPECTED BEYOND THE PANTH.` · `JEWELS IN EVERY MIND.` · then, large: `SCHOOLS, NOT ONLY TEMPLES.`

segments.voice: Two minutes for a classroom. Sit, and let your breath slow. Bring to mind a school you know: your own old one, your children's, a school down the street, a Punjabi or Sunday school at a gurdwara or church. Picture a single classroom in it, early in the morning, before anyone arrives. The chairs, the board, the smell of paper. Breathe in, and picture the children coming in. Breathe out, and wish them good teachers and open minds. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out. The bell holds the time.
Attar Singh, the holy man of Mastuana, a former soldier known for meditation and kirtan, who founded schools and a college so that learning grew beside faith. Today's word.
Your line: schools, not only temples. Today, support a school: donate supplies, help with homework, or offer an hour to a school near you. Day nine hundred ninety-four.
